Swiss stage, quarterfinals and semifinals at the Credit Union of Texas Event Center in Allen, Texas. Final on 14 November at Barclays Center, Brooklyn, New York City. 19 teams. Karmine Corp (French organisation, LEC) played its first World Championship. It came through the play-in (beat Cloud9 KIA 3-2, then MVK Esports 3-0 twice). body.input: Jane, the knockout stage is HERE! Eight teams, best-of-fives, and T1 hunting for a fourth title in a row!
Yes, Paul, and Gen.G and Dplus KIA also went three-and-oh in Swiss, so T1 aren’t exactly strolling in unnoticed.
But LYON made playoffs for the first time ever! That’s the dream! And they’re facing Gen.G on the fourth of November—what a way to start!
And Karmine Corp—first French org in knockouts since 2011. They scraped through play-ins, beat Cloud9 KIA three-two, then MVK Esports three-oh twice, and still finished Swiss at three-and-two.
And now they face T1 on the sixth of November. David versus Goliath, Jane! A French organisation against the three-time defending champions!
David had a sling. Karmine Corp’s sling is… a two-nil win over Movistar KOI and a two-nil over CTBC Flying Oyster? Not exactly legendary yet.
Oh come on, underdog magic is real! Five million dollar prize pool, single elimination, best-of-five—this is where legends are made!
Legends or not, the format doesn’t lie. One loss and you’re out. No second chances, no Swiss stage safety net.
But that’s what makes it thrilling! Dplus KIA versus Bilibili Gaming on the fifth, Top Esports versus Invictus Gaming on the third—every match is a war!
A war with facts. And so far, the facts say T1, Gen.G, and Dplus KIA are the ones to beat.
And Karmine Corp could be the story of the tournament! First French team in knockouts in over a decade—imagine if they take down T1!
Imagine if they don’t. Then it’s just another early exit for Europe.
Jane, you’re killing the vibe! Allen, Texas—get ready for fireworks!
We’ll be watching. And fact-checking. As always.
